# SOLTest player guide

Every control of the game and every element of the flight HUD, as the in-game Help page shows them (Esc, then Help). The keys are the default ones: rebind them in Settings, Key bindings, and the game's own pages and hints follow.

## Controls

### Flight

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>Mouse</kbd> | Steer while mouse steering is on: the mouse moves a virtual joystick (yaw and pitch rate; torque in manual flight). With it off the cursor is shown and stays inside the game window |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Steer with the mouse while held (the joystick recenters on press and release) |
| <kbd>MMB</kbd> | Mouse steering on / off (off at flight start unless Settings "Mouse steering at start" is on; the joystick recenters when it turns on or off) |
| <kbd>B</kbd> | Recenter the joystick (stop turning) |
| <kbd>W</kbd> / <kbd>S</kbd> | Thrust forward / backward |
| <kbd>A</kbd> / <kbd>D</kbd> | Strafe left / right |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> | Thrust up / down |
| <kbd>Q</kbd> / <kbd>E</kbd> | Roll left / right |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Boost on / off (turns off at a blackout, a jump and a respawn) |
| <kbd>C</kbd> | Assisted / manual flight (starts assisted unless turned off in Settings); during autopilot: take control in assisted flight |
| <kbd>Z</kbd> | Stop spin: cancel all rotation (hold) |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd> | Free-look around the ship (hold) |
| <kbd>Wheel</kbd> | Step the speed cap (10 notches per factor of ten) |
| <kbd>F3</kbd> | Speed panel: set the cap digit by digit or from a body's speed |

### Targeting

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>T</kbd> | Select the target nearest the reticle |
| <kbd>R</kbd> / <kbd>F</kbd> | Next farther / next nearer target |
| <kbd>X</kbd> | Clear the target |
| <kbd>M</kbd> | Lock the reference frame to the target (match its velocity) |
| <kbd>L</kbd> | Surface-lock: keep the ship upright over the nearest body |

### Combat

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>LMB</kbd> | Fire the pulse guns (hold). With mouse steering off, on an overlay icon: press, drag toward an action and release to choose it (release in the centre, or Esc, cancels) |
| <kbd>G</kbd> | Drop a practice target 200 m ahead |

### Time

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>[</kbd> / <kbd>]</kbd> | Time warp down / up |
| <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | Time warp back to 1x |

### Overlays

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>O</kbd> | Overlays on / off in the active profile: everything checked in the Overlay Menu together (saved with the profile) |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>O</kbd> | Orbit lines on / off in the active profile |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>O</kbd> | Overlay Menu: the five overlay profiles and what the overlay key shows in each (icons per kind, orbits per kind, ships on radar, darkening); also in Settings |
| <kbd>RShift</kbd>+<kbd>O</kbd> | Cycle overlay profiles (the enabled ones; also in the Overlay Menu) |

### HUD

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>-</kbd> / <kbd>=</kbd> | Radar range in / out (manual) |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> | Radar back to automatic range |

### Map

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>M</kbd> | Open the map in the last mode used / close it |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>J</kbd> | Open the map in Jump mode |
| <kbd>J</kbd> / <kbd>M</kbd> / <kbd>P</kbd> | Jump / Move / Patrol mode (P again: loop or ping-pong patrol) |
| <kbd>RMB</kbd> | Orbit the map camera (drag) |
| <kbd>RMB</kbd> | Click a body: its action menu (Up / Down and Enter, or click; Esc closes) |
| <kbd>MMB</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>RMB</kbd> | Pan the map (drag) |
| <kbd>Wheel</kbd> | Zoom the map |
| <kbd>LMB</kbd> | Pick a destination or add a waypoint: press on a body or space, drag, release |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>LMB</kbd> | Preview the height above the plane / lock it |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>RMB</kbd> | Undo the last waypoint (click) |
| <kbd>X</kbd> | Clear the destination and the planned waypoints |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Jump to the destination / start the route |
| <kbd>Delete</kbd> | Clear the active route |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Close the map |

### Routes

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>V</kbd> | Resume a paused route (in flight and on the map) |
| <kbd>P</kbd> | Show or hide routes in flight (the map always shows them) |

### Menu

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Stop a Chase Down; else pause menu (in flight) / close the open page, else resume |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>F1</kbd> | Same as Esc (temporary: Esc stops Play-In-Editor before the game sees it) |

### Demo

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>F2</kbd> | Show or hide the NPC stats overlay |

## HUD glossary

### Flight HUD

![Flight HUD](Images/33-help-glossary-flight-hud.png)

![Flight HUD, part 2 of 6](Images/33-help-glossary-flight-hud-2.png)

![Flight HUD, part 3 of 6](Images/33-help-glossary-flight-hud-3.png)

![Flight HUD, part 4 of 6](Images/33-help-glossary-flight-hud-4.png)

![Flight HUD, part 5 of 6](Images/33-help-glossary-flight-hud-5.png)

![Flight HUD, part 6 of 6](Images/33-help-glossary-flight-hud-6.png)

| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Reticle | Where the ship's nose points: your guns fire along it. Target selection (T) picks the target nearest to it. |
| Virtual joystick | The mouse is a virtual joystick: the dot is the stick and the farther it sits from the centre, the faster the ship turns. It recenters with B. While you hold Alt to look around the circles turn yellow, because the stick is frozen and the mouse moves the camera instead. |
| Mouse-steer icon | Shows whether the mouse is steering. An open arrow means it is not (you have a free cursor). A reticle means it steers while you hold Space, and a reticle with a small tick means it is locked on by MMB. The icon is bright while the mouse is steering and dim otherwise. |
| Prograde marker | A green circle with three ticks (left, right and up) that sits where you are heading, measured against the reference frame (the nearest body, or your locked target). Fly toward it to keep going the way you are going. It shows only above 0.1 m/s of relative speed. |
| Retrograde marker | A red-orange circle with a cross that sits exactly opposite your direction of travel. Point your nose at it and thrust to brake. Like the prograde marker it appears only once you are moving relative to the reference frame. |
| Flight mode | The last line of the speed card, under the speed bar, names the flight mode. ASSISTED (blue) holds the velocity your keys ask for, MANUAL (orange) fires the thrusters directly and keeps any spin until you hold Z, and AUTO (green) is the autopilot flying for you. Switch between the first two with C. Next to it the line reads BOOST while boost (Tab) is on, else boost off. |
| Speed card | The big number is your speed relative to the reference frame, with the frame's name under it ([M LOCK] when it is locked to your target) and your speed against the Sun beneath. The cap line and its bar show how much of your speed limit you use, orange when above it. Step the cap with the mouse wheel or set it with F3. |
| G meter | Shows the G force you feel and how much of your tolerance is left. Above 1.5 G the bar drains, harder pulls drain it faster, and it refills below that. Manual flight warns when you pass the limit, and at the combat limit of 9 G the meter empties in seconds and you black out. During a Chase Down, small ticks on the bar mark its floor and resume points. |
| Date and anchor card | Top left: the simulated date and the time-warp factor, the anchor (the body the world is centred on) and the nearest body, and the surface-lock state. Surface-lock (L) keeps the ship upright over the nearest body when you are close enough. |
| Key hints and notices | The hint lines at the screen edge remind you which keys do what right now. The steer hint appears until you first steer with the mouse, and a one-time notice appears after an update changed your default controls. Rebind keys in Settings and the hints follow. |
| Autopilot marker | At the top centre while the autopilot flies you: its target, the time to arrive and the distance. Any thrust, roll, steering or stop spin of yours, or C, takes control back in assisted flight at once. A key you were already holding counts only after you let it go. |
| Chase Down line | While a Chase Down runs, the autopilot marker becomes a chase marker with a second line naming what the ship is doing: BURST, COOL or BRAKE, and the G it uses. It never lets the G meter fall below your safety margin, 25 percent by default (set it in Settings). |
| Jump warp streaks | Streaks of light that rush past while a jump to a map destination plays. The jump takes a few seconds, and you arrive at the destination's position at the end of it. |

### Targets and radar

![Targets and radar](Images/33-help-glossary-targets-radar.png)

![Targets and radar, part 2 of 3](Images/33-help-glossary-targets-radar-2.png)

![Targets and radar, part 3 of 3](Images/33-help-glossary-targets-radar-3.png)

| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Target bracket and name | A bracket drawn around the selected target with its name and distance under it. Select the target nearest the reticle with T, step farther or nearer with R and F, and clear it with X. |
| Off-screen target arrow | When the target is outside the view, an orange arrow near the screen edge points toward it. Turn that way and the arrow becomes the bracket. |
| Target card | Top right: the target's name, its distance and its velocity relative to you. Lock the reference frame to it with M to match its velocity, which makes closing in on it easy. |
| Radar scope | A 3D scope at the bottom right. The disc is your ship's own plane with forward at the top, the rings mark a quarter, half, three quarters and all of the range, and the pulse sweeping outward is for show. The wedge is your camera's view. In AUTO the range is 10,000 km, tightening to 1 km when you select a target. - and = zoom by ten (MANUAL) and Home returns to AUTO. |
| Contact above the plane | A blue dot on a solid stem: the object is above your ship's plane (or on it). The stem is its height and the short tick at the foot is its position straight under it. |
| Contact below the plane | An orange hollow ring on a dashed stem: the object is below your ship's plane. Contacts behind you are dimmer, and ones past the range are pulled in to the edge of the range along their true direction and drawn dimmer still. |
| Selected target on the radar | Your selected target is drawn larger with a highlight ring and its name beside it, so you can find it among the other contacts. |

### Overlays and route

![Overlays and route](Images/33-help-glossary-overlays-route.png)

![Overlays and route, part 2 of 5](Images/33-help-glossary-overlays-route-2.png)

![Overlays and route, part 3 of 5](Images/33-help-glossary-overlays-route-3.png)

![Overlays and route, part 4 of 5](Images/33-help-glossary-overlays-route-4.png)

![Overlays and route, part 5 of 5](Images/33-help-glossary-overlays-route-5.png)

| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Star icon | A yellow ring crossed by rays marks a star. Overlay icons are hologram markers that show where things are; switch them with O or choose kinds in the Overlay Menu (Ctrl+O). |
| Planet icon | A plain ring marks a planet. Point at it with the mouse free and press LMB to open its action menu and choose what to do with it. |
| Moon icon | A smaller ring marks a moon, so it reads as a satellite of the planet it circles. |
| Dwarf planet icon | A diamond marks a dwarf planet such as Pluto or Ceres. |
| Asteroid icon | A triangle marks one of the fifty largest named asteroids. |
| Ring system icon | An ellipse around a planet's icon marks its ring system. It shows only together with the planet icons. |
| NPC ship icon | A green chevron marks a ship flown by the simulation. Only the nearest ones get an icon, and the same ships can appear as radar contacts. |
| Practice target icon | An orange square marks a practice target. Drop one ahead of you with G and shoot it with LMB. |
| Off-screen icon arrows | An icon that is outside the view becomes a small chevron just inside the screen edge, pointing toward the object. Only the nearest few get one. |
| Distance darkening | With darkening on (a row of the Overlay Menu), far icons dim so near ones stand out. Icons also fade as the object itself grows on screen: brightest while it is smaller than about 6 pixels in radius and gone once it is big enough to see for itself. |
| Orbit lines<br>![Orbit lines](Images/33-glossary-crop-orbit-lines.png) | Lines that trace the orbits of planets, dwarf planets, moons and the largest asteroids. The selected target's orbit is drawn in gold. Switch them with Alt+O. |
| Overlay profile tag | Shows for a moment which of the 5 overlay profiles is active whenever you cycle profiles with RShift+O. Each profile remembers its own overlay choices. |
| Route legs<br>![Route legs](Images/33-glossary-crop-route-legs.png) | Your planned route as glow lines with arrows that fade from dim at the start to bright at the end. On a patrol loop the closing leg back to the first waypoint is dashed. Show or hide routes in flight with P; the map always shows them. |
| Waypoints<br>![Waypoints](Images/33-glossary-crop-waypoints.png) | A route's stops. A stop above the level plane through your ship (on the map, the grid's plane) is a blue ring with a dot in it, one below it a hollow orange ring. On the map a stop clearly off that plane also has a stem to the grid in the same colour. |
| Route progress line | Shows the kind of route. A move shows the leg you are flying, how much of the route is done and the time to its end; a patrol shows the next waypoint and the time to reach it. When a route is paused, V re-plans it from where you are and resumes. |
| Space dust | Faint specks drifting around the ship. They are not objects: they only make your speed visible when everything else is far away. Turn them off in Settings, Graphics. |

### Menus and map

![Menus and map](Images/33-help-glossary-menus-map.png)

![Menus and map, part 2 of 3](Images/33-help-glossary-menus-map-2.png)

![Menus and map, part 3 of 3](Images/33-help-glossary-menus-map-3.png)

| Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Icon hover and radial menu | Point at an overlay icon with the mouse free and it turns orange with a highlight ring. Press LMB on it to open the radial menu with its name and actions, drag toward one and release to choose it. Release in the centre, or press Esc, to cancel. An action that cannot run says why. |
| Info card | Choosing Info on an object opens its card at the top right for 10 seconds: name, type, distance, details and its current status. |
| Overlay Menu | A hologram checklist (Ctrl+O) with a tab for each of the 5 overlay profiles. Choose which icons, orbit lines, radar ships and darkening each profile shows. Enable more profiles and cycle them with RShift+O. |
| Speed panel | Opened with F3: type your speed cap digit by digit, or pick a body from the list to set the cap to its orbital speed. Changes apply to the ship at once. |
| Hologram mouse pointer | The mouse pointer everywhere in the game is a small glowing hologram arrow instead of the Windows arrow. Its jitter follows the Hologram menu effects slider in Settings. |
| Map body icons | On the map each body is an icon with its name. Open the map with Shift+M, or in Jump mode with Shift+J. Zoom with the mouse wheel and drag with the right button to turn the view. |
| Map destination pick<br>![Map destination pick](Images/33-glossary-crop-map-pick.png) | Press on a body or on empty space, drag and release to place a destination. A disc shows the direction and range, a guide line the height above or below the plane, and a marker the spot. Hold Shift to set the height, then click to lock it. The hint line says what to do next. |
| Map grid and stems<br>![Map grid and stems](Images/33-glossary-crop-map-grid.png) | A flat grid, level with the plane of the planets, through the point the map turns around, with a stem from each marked point down or up to it, so you can read where something is above or below the grid. |
| Map action list | Right-click a body on the map for its action menu: choose with Up and Down and Enter, or click, and Esc closes it. The same actions as the icons' radial menu, as a list. |
